key_insight: A trained ReLU network defines a Data Information Matrix distribution that, after modification on a measure-zero set, induces a singular foliation of input space.
engineering_relevance: This framework offers a theoretical lens for studying how trained networks organize input geometry, rather than a ready-to-use engineering method.
method: Define an input-space distribution using the columns of the Data Information Matrix.
Prove that the ReLU-induced distribution is non-smooth.
Construct a smoothed distribution differing only on a measure-zero set and prove it induces a singular foliation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical proofs, with no datasets, empirical benchmarks, or quantitative evaluations described.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish how to compute or validate the resulting foliation efficiently for practical networks.
paper_title: The Geometry of Manifold Learning: Singular foliations via Deep Learning models
